PullRequest.Title: Agent Host: replace unacknowledged send_message queued messages and keep the session model
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #339099

## Summary

When sessions talk to each other, the sender now reads the latest state and keeps one complete, up-to-date message in the target. Before, each `send_message` or `send_remote_message` call to a busy chat queued another unread message. Editing a queued cross-session message also shows the session's model in the picker instead of **Auto**.

### A follow-up replaces the sender's unacknowledged message

- If the target chat is busy and the sending chat already has a queued message there that hasn't started, the new message replaces it instead of queuing another turn. Both tool descriptions tell the model to write one complete message that reflects the current state, not only what changed.
- `get_session_context` returns the caller's undelivered message in full as `yourUndeliveredMessage`. Only the caller's own message is included; other senders' and user-queued messages are not.
- Both tools return the replaced text (`send_message` in its result text, `send_remote_message` as `replacedMessage` with status `replaced`), so the agent can see whether it dropped anything it still needs.
- The message keeps its ID, place in the queue, origin, model, and agent, and its delegation metadata points at the sender's latest turn. Attachments are kept, but their text ranges are removed because they pointed into the old text.
- **Fallback when the message already started:**
  - Local `send_message` reads and replaces in one synchronous host step, so it either replaces the waiting message or queues a new one.
  - Remote `send_remote_message` reuses the waiting message's ID. `ChatPendingMessageSet` is an upsert, so if the host started the earlier message before the replacement arrived, the replacement is queued as a new message. Nothing is lost or delivered twice, and the host needs no protocol change.
  - The router reports `replaced` only when the earlier message was still waiting. If it saw the message start or get removed first, it reports `queued`.
- **User edits:** editing a queued message in VS Code re-sends it as a new user message, so after a user edit the agent's follow-up queues separately instead of overwriting the user's change.

### Model handling

- Agent-sent queued messages carry no model, as before, so each runs on whatever model the target chat is using when it starts and never switches it. This matches the immediate-send path, which has never set a model. (An earlier revision of this PR filled in a model when the message was queued. That was removed because it could go stale: a reordered queue, a provider fallback, or a model becoming unavailable would make delivery switch models or fail the turn.)
- Inline-editing any request with no recorded model now starts on the conversation's current model and configuration, such as Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M, instead of the inline editor's default, Auto. Before, resubmitting that edit switched the chat to Auto and broke the prompt cache.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, start a long-running task in session **B** with a non-default model, for example Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M.
2. From session **A**, ask the agent to `send_message` session B, then send an update while B is still busy.
3. B shows one queued message from A containing only the latest complete message, and A's result includes the text it replaced.
4. From A, call `get_session_context` on B. The result includes `yourUndeliveredMessage`.
5. Edit that queued message (pencil icon). The model picker shows B's model, not Auto.
6. Let B finish. The message runs as one turn on B's model, and A's next message queues a fresh message.
7. Repeat steps 2–3 across hosts with `send_remote_message`. The second call reports `"status":"replaced"`.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/{sessionServerTools,serverToolGroups,agentService,agentSideEffects}.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/remoteSessions/test/{browser,common}/*.test.ts` (files listed explicitly): passed (1217 passing). The remote fallback test fails if the router's "earlier message already left the queue" detection is disabled.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWidget.test.ts`: passed (56 passing). The new inline-edit test fails without the `chatWidget.ts` change.
- `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts`: regenerated the 19 Copilot prompt snapshots for the new `send_message` and `get_session_context` descriptions (description lines only). A plain replay run then passed (23 passing).
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/{copilot,claude,codex}AgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "server tool"`: passed (Copilot 40, Claude 33 + 6 existing skips, Codex 40).
- `node build/checker/layersChecker.ts`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed files. The local run, like the type-check step of `valid-layers-check`, reports only pre-existing missing `electron` typings in this worktree.
- `npx eslint` on changed files: clean.
- **Live run with real models** (`validate-ui-scenario`, Code OSS dev build 1.141.0, macOS arm64, local agent host, Copilot): **passed, 7/7 steps**.
  - Session B: Claude Opus 5.5 · High · 1M, running `sleep 240`.
  - Agent A called `send_message` twice, 4 seconds apart, 17 seconds into B's sleep. The second call returned `Message replaced this chat's undelivered queued message (…). Replaced message: PLAN-V1: …`, and `get_session_context` returned `yourUndeliveredMessage: PLAN-V2: …`.
  - B's **Queued** section held exactly one message (PLAN-V2).
  - The inline editor for that message showed `Claude Opus 5.5 · Thinking Level: High, Context Size: 1M`, matching B's picker (not Auto).
  - After the sleep, PLAN-V2 was delivered exactly once ("Sent by another session") and answered. PLAN-V1 was never delivered, and B's model and configuration were unchanged (no model change in `agenthost.log`).
  - Not covered live: the cross-host `send_remote_message` path, which needs a second, remote agent host. It is covered by router tests that use the protocol reducer.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The raw-text insertion, lack of an input maximum, established transcript caps, and model-facing return path are directly visible. The prevalence of very long messages is uncertain, but byte/token scaling is not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Tool-result bytes and model prompt tokens allocated, JSON-encoded, and sent to the provider.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(L × C) extra bytes/tokens for message length L and context/replacement call count C; unlike transcript data, L is not capped by detail or transcriptLimit.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased model-request payload and latency, plus serialization/allocation pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Previously, get_session_context contained only a bounded transcript and send_message returned only a short status/link; queued text was not duplicated into either model-facing result.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A context read, and every successful replacement, now copies the entire previous queued message into a tool result that becomes model input, bypassing the serializer's existing per-detail caps.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1493 adds `undelivered.message.text` directly to the model-facing JSON after transcript fields have been truncated by `contextCaps`; RIGHT line 1327 also interpolates the complete replaced text into the send_message result. Neither path applies a length bound, and the send_message schema has no `maxLength`.
Findings.Title: Cap queued-message text before returning it to the model
Findings.Impact: A detailed status, log, or code message can dominate the compact summary and add thousands or more prompt bytes before the next model response. Repeated checks or replacements increase provider upload, token processing, latency, and allocation linearly.
Findings.Evidence: `serializeSessionContext` truncates transcript messages using `contextCaps` and caps the window at 50, but `yourUndeliveredMessage` uses raw queued text. The new test verifies that a 5,008-character message remains intact even in `summary`, where user text is otherwise capped at 160 characters. `applyGetSessionContextTool` returns this JSON as the server-tool result, so the bytes are serialized and included on the next model-provider request; repeated checks repeat the payload. The replacement formatter creates the same uncapped copy on send.
Findings.Recommendation: Return a bounded preview with original length and truncation metadata. If full recovery is required, expose it only through an explicit opt-in/full-detail path with a documented maximum rather than bypassing summary and digest caps.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Repeated send_message calls to a busy target previously appended a fresh pending message each time. After the active turn completed, the queue drain serialized all of those stale entries into separate full agent/provider turns, multiplying model/network work and delaying the latest update linearly with the number of follow-ups.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Busy target chats could accumulate many stale same-sender turns, causing avoidable LLM requests and making the final/current update wait behind all earlier follow-ups.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Same-sender follow-ups now reuse and replace the sender's existing undelivered queue entry, bounding that sender to one pending provider turn while preserving FIFO position and separate messages from other senders.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, every busy-target send_message dispatches ChatPendingMessageSet with a fresh generateUuid() id, so the reducer appends each follow-up. QueueDrainContribution consumes queuedMessages[0] after each successful turn and calls host.sendTurnMessage for every entry, making each stale follow-up a separate provider/model turn. The changed path finds the same source chat's still-undelivered entry and dispatches ChatPendingMessageSet with that existing id, which the reducer upserts in place; tests establish that multiple same-sender sends leave one queued message while different senders remain distinct.

Scenarios.Scenario: A local agent sends repeated updates to a busy same-host target chat.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool waits for the existing listSessions lookup, then synchronously reads and dispatches target state before returning. Provider execution is intentionally off this immediate critical path while the target is busy; after the active turn, queue drain must complete one provider turn before the next.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch ChatPendingMessageSet to host state and connected protocol consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host state/protocol action per send, unchanged; after coalescing, one eventual provider turn per source chat's currently pending message instead of one turn per same-source follow-up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each send dispatched the same action but always used a fresh ID, appending another queue entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: State dispatch is on the send tool's critical path; the provider/model request is deferred until the busy target drains and determines how long the latest message waits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send each admitted queued turn to the agent/model provider through host.sendTurnMessage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For F sequential follow-ups from one source while busy, one provider turn after the diff versus F before; K distinct senders can still produce K turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every fresh-ID follow-up was eventually sent as a separate provider turn; the diff replaces same-source waiting entries in place.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the sender tool's immediate path, but serialized on the target chat's progress and therefore controls when the current update is processed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of same-source follow-ups sent while a target turn remains active, after grouping by source chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The read/replace/dispatch section has no await and is atomic on the host event loop. Queue drain admits one turn at a time. Effective queued provider cardinality is now one pending entry per source chat, plus entries from other sources, rather than one per follow-up.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The target chat and queue are read from the in-memory AgentHostStateManager; there is no result cache or negative cache. Each send scans the currently materialized queue once. A replacement updates the existing queue entry, so warm/cold cache behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fresh-ID append, reducer upsert semantics, serial queue drain, and provider dispatch were all traced; the fixing introducer was resolved and recorded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of follow-ups and provider cost vary by workflow, but the before/after turn-count reduction is exact.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance-positive overall: it removes repeated queued model turns. The small O(queue length) sender lookup introduces no expensive boundary and is outweighed by coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat sends or replaces a message on a connected remote agent host.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connection validation, session/chat state availability, workspace trust checks, background chat acquisition, remote dispatch, and acknowledgement must finish before the send tool returns. The later provider turn remains off the send critical path when queued.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to remote session/chat state, dispatch ChatPendingMessageSet, and wait for the matching accepted action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two state subscriptions/read waits plus one remote action dispatch and acknowledgement per send, unchanged by the diff; warm subscriptions can satisfy state reads from verifiedValue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscriptions, trust checks, dispatch, and acknowledgement occurred; only the dispatched ID/message now upserts an observed same-source waiting entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These connected-host IPC/network operations are on the send tool's critical path until acknowledgement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run admitted remote queued messages as provider/model turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One eventual provider turn per effective queued entry; sequential same-source follow-ups collapse to one, while different source chats remain separate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each remote send used a fresh ID and therefore caused a separate later provider turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred from the send acknowledgement but serialized on target-chat completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Remote send count, effective distinct source chats, and whether follow-ups arrive before the prior queue entry starts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent sends can execute concurrently without a global limiter. Sequential same-source sends observed in current state replace by ID; simultaneous sends may each dispatch, but this does not make behavior worse than the base. The remote host reducer serializes received actions and queue drain runs one target turn at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm remote subscription exposes `verifiedValue`; a cold send awaits existing session/chat subscription state. The diff reads that already-subscribed state and adds no separate fetch or cache. There is no cross-call coalescing cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: subscription state, dispatch/ack listener lifecycle, ID reuse, fallback when the old ID starts, and cleanup in finally were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote RTT and follow-up frequency vary; action count remains one per send, while eventual model-turn savings depend on sequential updates arriving before queue drain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced boundary regression. The diff uses existing subscribed state and the same one-dispatch acknowledgement path, while reducing later provider work for observed sequential follow-ups.

Scenarios.Scenario: A sender calls get_session_context while its detailed message is still queued.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: listSessions, chat-state resolution, transcript serialization, and the returned tool result must complete before the calling model can continue. The returned bytes then join the next provider request, so result size is on the model-response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-encode uncapped `yourUndeliveredMessage` alongside the otherwise capped transcript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model-facing tool result and one subsequent provider request per context call; the new extra payload is the full undelivered-message length on every call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The result contained at most 50 turns with 160/300/1000-character user caps by detail and no queued-message field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization completes before tool return, and all result bytes are included before the model can produce its next response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry the server-tool JSON into the calling agent's next model-provider request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider upload per subsequent model continuation, with O(L) additional bytes for undelivered length L each time context is checked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the capped compact transcript and fixed metadata were carried.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Larger prompt upload and token processing delay the next model response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Undelivered message length L multiplied by number of context reads C; queue cardinality only affects a linear lookup, not returned-message count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each tool invocation serializes independently; repeated or parallel context checks are not coalesced. Queue lookup is one linear scan of the effective pending queue per call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The default target chat is read from in-memory state; a specific peer chat may use the existing resolveChatState path. No serialization cache exists, so every call rebuilds and JSON-encodes the payload, including the same undelivered text.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the uncapped raw insertion occurs after explicit transcript caps and returns directly as model-facing JSON. Only prevalence and exact latency are uncertain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical delegated-message lengths and context-check frequency are not measured; the test establishes at least a 5,008-character uncapped case, and the schema permits longer inputs.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: the new full-text field defeats the serializer's compactness bounds and repeats unbounded bytes/tokens on a critical model path.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user inline-edits a queued agent-authored request that has no recorded model.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On the user's edit click, the inline editor is created and a programmatic model selection is requested. The call is not awaited; edit rendering and focus continue without waiting for model resolution.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user-initiated inline edits and model catalog size for the local linear lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request is made per edit action. The controller owns a single pending programmatic selection and clears/replaces the prior pending request, preventing accumulation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing model catalog and per-editor model configuration store are used. The current conversation model should normally be warm; if not yet published, the existing programmatic-selection controller waits for catalog reconciliation. No new network or filesystem cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: requestModelByIdentifier resolves from the existing in-memory model pool and selection controller; no changed remote boundary was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size and UI hardware vary, but the changed work is a local model-list lookup/configuration-store read and is not awaited.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added local lookup runs once per explicit edit, is asynchronous from rendering, and pending selection is coalesced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 28 changed files and every diff page. Submitted one medium serialization/network finding for uncapped queued-message text in model-facing results. Also recorded the PR's high-confidence fix for stale same-sender queued turns multiplying provider requests; no other diff-caused performance regressions were established.
